> [L2]   "content": "# The Corykidion\n\nA small, local-first, read-only-first bridge between AI agents and [TheBrain](https://www.thebrain.com/).\n\nIt talks to TheBrain's desktop app over its local HTTP API — which is only reachable while the app is open on your machine. It can check that a Brain is open, look up a Thought, search by name, retrieve a Thought's full context (parents, children, jumps, links, attachments) and notes, check recent activity, and export a deterministic snapshot. It also has a write pipeline — attaching URLs, activating Thoughts, and creating Thoughts — that is fully built and unit-tested but has not yet been run against a real Brain. Every capability this package does not fully support is documented as unsupported rather than left ambiguous.\n\nNot affiliated with or endorsed by TheBrain Technologies.\n\n## Why this exists\n\nBefore any code was written, this project surveyed eighteen public repositories that touch TheBrain in some way — MCP servers, SDKs, migration scripts, a PowerShell audit tool, a UUID codec — to determine which ideas were worth building on. That survey is preserved in full in [`WORKING_ARCHITECTURE.md`](WORKING_ARCHITECTURE.md): what each repository got right, what it got wrong, and what specifically was worth reusing versus rejecting. No code from those eighteen repositories was copied into this one. A small number of design patterns were reused, with attribution recorded in the ledger; most repositories contributed nothing directly.\n\nSummary of what that survey found: most of the eighteen repositories are bound to TheBrain's *cloud* API, which cannot reach a Brain that exists only on your machine. Several write directly to TheBrain's private files, which risks corrupting the Brain's stored data. One official repository — [`TheBrainTech/send-to-thebrain`](https://github.com/TheBrainTech/send-to-thebrain) — was judged the most reliable foundation: it is TheBrain's own reference implementation of the local API, and this package's client is built directly against the endpoints that repository documents.\n\n## What actually works right now\n\n### Reads\n\nEvery read below has been verified against a real, running TheBrain instance, not just against fixtures.\n\n| Capability | What it does |\n|---|---|\n| `status` | Confirms TheBrain's desktop app is reachable, reports which Brain is currently open, and lists every Brain visible on the machine. |\n| `thought get` | Retrieves one Thought by ID: its name and label. |\n| `thought find-url` | Checks whether a URL is already attached to something in a Brain, using the same duplicate-detection approach as the official browser extension, so you don't create the same Thought twice. |\n| `thought search` | Searches Thoughts by name/label within a Brain. |\n| `thought graph` | Retrieves a Thought's full context in one call: identity, parents, children, jumps, links, and attachment metadata. |\n| `thought notes` | Retrieves a Thought's note content. |\n| `activity` | Lists a Brain's recent modification-log entries, newest first. |\n| `export thought` | Writes a deterministic, provenance-stamped JSON snapshot of one Thought. This is a projection for inspection, not a backup — TheBrain's own dated backups remain the source of truth. |\n| `capabilities` | Lists exactly what's implemented versus what's planned, so you (or an agent) never have to guess. |\n\nTwo capabilities remain unresolved even after live testing: `thought.links` and `thought.neighbors` are retired as separate operations, because `thought graph`'s response already contains both (TheBrain's link model is parent/child/jump, so links and neighbors are the same data). Calling either old name now points you to `thought graph` instead of failing silently.\n\n### Writes\n\nA write pipeline exists — plan, explicit approval, journal, apply, read-back verification — implemented in `src/corykidion/operations.py` and covered by unit tests against fabricated fixtures. It has not been run against a real Brain.\n\n| Capability | What it does | Status |\n|---|---|---|\n| `write attach-url` | Attaches a URL to a Thought. | Route and parameters documented by TheBrain's own reference client; not yet exercised live. |\n| `write activate` | Activates (opens/focuses) a Thought. | Route documented by TheBrain's own reference client; not yet exercised live. Verification is Brain-level only — no evidenced endpoint currently exposes which specific Thought is active. |\n| Create a Thought | Available as a library call (`WriteOperations.plan_create_thought`), not exposed on the CLI yet. | The route is documented; the request body schema is not verified against a real instance. The caller must supply the complete body explicitly — this package will not guess field names for a write. |\n\nBoth CLI write subcommands require `--approve` and `--journal PATH` explicitly. There is no default-approve path, and no write happens without both.\n\nTwo more writes described in the design ledger — appending a note and creating a link directly — have no verified request shape at all and are not implemented.\n\nRun `corykidion capabilities` for the live, authoritative list of what's evidenced versus what's still unverified.\n\n## Installing it\n\nYou need Python 3.11 or later and a running copy of TheBrain's desktop app (version 15.0.534+, which is when the local API shipped).\n\n```bash\ngit clone https://github.com/Corykidios/the_corykidion.git\ncd the_corykidion\npython -m venv .venv\n.venv\\Scripts\\activate      # Windows\n# source .venv/bin/activate # macOS/Linux\npip install -e \".[dev]\"\n```\n\nThen find your local API endpoint and key: open TheBrain, go to **Settings → User → Local API**, and copy both the endpoint (something like `http://localhost:52341/api`) and the API key.\n\nSet them as environment variables:\n\n```bash\nset CORYKIDION_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:52341/api      # Windows (cmd)\nset CORYKIDION_API_KEY=your-key-here\n\n$env:CORYKIDION_ENDPOINT = \"http://localhost:52341/api\" # Windows (PowerShell)\n$env:CORYKIDION_API_KEY = \"your-key-here\"\n```\n\n...or copy [`examples/config.example.toml`](examples/config.example.toml) to `config.toml` (already `.gitignore`'d — it will never accidentally get committed) and fill in your own values.\n\nThen:\n\n```bash\ncorykidion status\n```\n\nIf TheBrain isn't running, you'll get a plain-English error telling you so, not a stack trace.\n\n## Using it\n\n```bash\n# What's open, what's visible\ncorykidion status\n\n# One Thought, by Brain ID and Thought ID\ncorykidion thought get <brain-id> <thought-id>\n\n# Has this URL already been captured somewhere in this Brain?\ncorykidion thought find-url <brain-id> \"https://example.com/some-article\"\n\n# A deterministic JSON snapshot of one Thought\ncorykidion export thought <brain-id> <thought-id> out/thought.json\n\n# What's implemented vs. still candidate\ncorykidion capabilities\n\n# Restrict every operation to a specific Brain, refusing anything else\ncorykidion --allow-brain <brain-id> status\n```\n\nIt's also a plain Python library, if you'd rather call it from your own agent code than shell out:\n\n```python\nfrom corykidion.client import LocalBrainClient\nfrom corykidion.config import load_config\nfrom corykidion.read import ReadModel\n\nconfig = load_config()  # reads env vars, or pass a path to a TOML file\nread_model = ReadModel(LocalBrainClient(config))\n\nstatus = read_model.connectivity()\nprint(f\"{status.brain_count} brains visible, active: {status.active_brain_id}\")\n```\n\n## How it's put together\n\nA configuration boundary that keeps your endpoint and API key out of source control; a minimal HTTP client that speaks exactly the documented endpoints and nothing else; a capability registry that fails closed on anything unverified and flags which operations mutate data; a safety gate that enforces target scope and, for writes, requires explicit opt-in independent of whatever transport is calling it; a read model and a write-operations pipeline (plan, approve, journal, apply, verify) built on top of that; and a CLI. Every one of those pieces is unit-tested against fabricated fixtures — the test suite never touches a real network socket or a real Brain.\n\n```text\nsrc/corykidion/\n  config.py         configuration boundary — env vars or a gitignored TOML file\n  client.py         the local API client — eleven evidenced endpoints, stdlib only\n  capabilities.py   the evidenced/candidate registry — fails closed by design\n  safety.py         target-scope and write-gate enforcement, independent of transport\n  read.py           the agent-facing read model\n  operations.py     the Phase 2 write pipeline: plan, approve, journal, apply, verify\n  export.py         deterministic, provenance-stamped JSON export\n  cli.py            the CLI transport\ntests/\n  contract/         client, capability, read-model, export, and operations tests\n  safety/           config and safety-gate tests\n  fixtures/         fabricated responses — nothing here is a real Brain\n```\n\nRun the tests yourself:\n\n```bash\npytest\n```\n\nFor the full reasoning behind these choices — including the fifteen safety invariants this package holds itself to, why certain donor-repository patterns were adopted or rejected, and exactly what was and wasn't verified against a real running instance — see:\n\n- [`WORKING_ARCHITECTURE.md`](WORKING_ARCHITECTURE.md) — the living design ledger, including the capability-scope decisions.\n- [`docs/decisions/0002-live-verified-read-capabilities.md`](docs/decisions/0002-live-verified-read-capabilities.md) — what was verified live against a running local API, what was probed and blocked, and how the write pipeline is scoped.\n\nThe short version of the safety posture: loopback-only by default, read-only by default, no ambient targets (every call names its Brain explicitly), no writing to TheBrain's private files under any circumstances, and no transport — CLI, library, or a future MCP server — is ever allowed more authority than the core safety gate grants it.\n\n## What this is not\n\n- Not a replacement for TheBrain, its sync service, or its native backups.\n- Not a credential broker, a SQLite writer, or an autonomous bulk editor.\n- Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by TheBrain Technologies.\n- Not finished. Read `corykidion capabilities` before assuming something works.\n\n## Contributing to it\n\nTwo things are most useful right now. First, capturing the request body TheBrain's own desktop app sends when creating a Thought by hand (so `thought.create`'s write body can be verified instead of left as a caller-supplied dict). Second, running one supervised live write — `write attach-url` or `write activate` — against a disposable test Brain, with `--approve` and a real journal file, to confirm the write pipeline behaves the same outside of fixtures as it does inside them. Either way: capture the real shape, turn it into a fixture, add a contract test, and only then promote the capability (the procedure is documented in `capabilities.py`). Adding an endpoint without a fixture and a test is exactly the pattern this project surveyed eighteen other repositories to avoid repeating.\n\n## License\n\nMIT. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE).\n",

> # Holonic Anatomy and Attribution
> 
> ## Research Maps, Sixty-Term Outlines, Draft Essays, and Revised Final Essays
> 
> **Project-sourced working packet — 1 August 2026**
> 
> This packet completes six stages of work:
> 
> 1. reconstruct the Twelve-Part Anatomy of a holon;
> 2. reconstruct the Twelve-Property Attribution of a holon;
> 3. place all sixty Greek-anchored terms from the Holonic Object System into two essay outlines;
> 4. draft both essays;
> 5. review, revise, and enrich the Anatomy essay;
> 6. review, revise, and enrich the Attribution essay.
> 
> The source hierarchy used here is deliberate. Cory's direct explanations and corrections govern. The extracted sixty-term glossary supplies the English–Greek term pairs, but not automatically their definitions. AI-generated lectures and later reviews are supporting evidence: useful where they clarify Cory's account, quarantined where they add metaphors, requirements, or system language he rejected.
> 
> The Greek forms are therefore treated as **controlled-vocabulary anchors and poetic color** copied from the project record. This packet does not claim that each is a literal dictionary translation of its English partner.
> 
> ### Editorial rulings
> 
> - **Explanation, not Expression, belongs to the anatomy.** The sixty-term extraction includes **expression [ἀπαγγελία]**, but Cory later identified it as an AI-amplified relic of an earlier slip in which he had used *expression* where he meant *explanation*. Expression remains in the sixty-term audit because it is present in the historical list; it is not promoted into a thirteenth anatomical part.
> - **Awakened is the current property; Arrived is the legacy term.** The extracted list contains **arrived [ποιέω]**. The current revision uses **Awakened** for the immutable first timestamp because it better names the event. Arrived remains visible as the source-era alias, pending any later decision about its Greek anchor.
> - **The current Being order is Name, Type, Nature, Tags.** Several older lectures printed Name, Nature, Type, Tags. The order stated for this assignment governs this packet.
> - **Will, Mind, Form, and Soul are not four individual holon types.** They are source-era names for four families or internal systems containing twelve types each. Will is certainly not a type. Mind and Soul were already under reconsideration because those words acquired controlled uses elsewhere.
> - **Tetrad is preferred over band.** The properties form three tetrads: Being, Bonding, and Becoming.
> - **Anatomical parts are potential, not twelve mandatory filled boxes.** Every holon shares the same possible anatomy. A valid holon does not need a Nature, Explanation, Extension, Reference, Relevancy, Definition, or Description.
> 
> ### Primary project evidence read
> 
> - `workmeri_chatgpt_1.md`: the extracted sixty-term list and Cory's direct explanations of Groups I–V.
> - `protocore_claude_3.md`: the three-lecture review, Cory's detailed corrections, the repeated sixty-term extraction, and Core's comparative synthesis.
> - `protocore_claude_1.md`: the earlier basis-centered knowledge-graph account and the short/strict Name versus long/slack Nature distinction.
> - The remaining supplied project records were searched for corroborating Holonics references and later uses of the system.

> # Stage One — Knowledge Map of the Twelve-Part Anatomy
> 
> ## 1. The governing idea
> 
> A **holon [ὅλον]** is the basic information object in Holonics. It is simultaneously a **whole [ὅλος]**, because it may contain other holons, and a **part [ὄζος]**, because it may participate within one or more containing holons. Whole and Part are roles, not mutually exclusive species.
> 
> A **hierarchy [ἰεραρχία]** records the vertical Whole–Part relation: Parents above, Children below. A **holarchy [ὅλαρχία]** includes those vertical relations without pretending they exhaust reality. It also permits more than one Parent, co-membership among Siblings, and other Relations among Relatives. Hierarchy survives inside holarchy; it simply loses its claim to be the only shape that matters.
> 
> At the deepest level, everything in this information theory is an **object [πρᾶγμα]**. When substantially represented in an account or database, an object may appear as an object proper, a relation, or an attribute. Holonics can then treat even a relation or attribute as a holon when it needs to be named, discussed, stored, or related in its own right.
> 
> ## 2. The twelve parts as six alliterative pairs
> 
> The count is easiest to remember as six pairs, but the structure is nested rather than flat.
> 
> | Pair | Function | Structural location |
> | --- | --- | --- |
> | **Name & Nature** | short identification and optional long content | the two great surfaces of a holon |
> | **Marker & Moniker** | logical threshold and lexical body | the two required features of the Name |
> | **Code & Cord** | encoded pattern and terminating boundary | the two features of the Marker |
> | **Explanation & Extension** | primary content and connective content | two interpretive functions within one Nature field |
> | **Reference & Relevancy** | outward citation and inward reading guidance | two kinds of Extension |
> | **Definition & Description** | inline explanation and bracketed alternative attribution | optional features nested in lexical territory, chiefly the Moniker |
> 
> ```mermaid
> flowchart TD
>     H["Holon"] --> N["Name — required"]
>     H --> T["Nature — optional"]
>     N --> M["Marker"]
>     N --> O["Moniker"]
>     M --> C["Code"]
>     M --> D["Cord"]
>     O -.-> F["Definition — optional"]
>     O -.-> S["Description — optional"]
>     T --> E["Explanation"]
>     T --> X["Extension"]
>     X --> R["Reference"]
>     X --> V["Relevancy"]
> ```
> 
> The diagram shows containment, not twelve separate database columns. In particular, Explanation and Extension may be recognized within one continuous Nature. A heading can mark their shift, but no compulsory field boundary divides them.
> 
> ## 3. Name and Nature
> 
> The **Name [φάτις]** is mandatory. It is one line, tends toward brevity, and leans toward **strict [σκληρός]** formatting because its Marker must be legible to the notation. It is what a person sees in the graph and what an account uses to address the holon.
> 
> The **Nature [φύσις]** is optional. It is the potentially multi-line body of content and leans toward **slack [ὀλίγος]** formatting. *Slack* does not mean careless. It means that a local style, best practice, or domain convention may govern the prose without every deviation breaking the object.
> 
> This is a gradient, not a crude law saying “Name strict, Nature slack.” Most absolute rules cluster in the Marker and in a few metadata delimiters. The Moniker is lexically free. The Nature may adopt strict conventions when a task benefits from them.
> 
> A useful diagnostic survives from Cory's direct account: when a Name grows so long that it wraps down the page, the problem may not be “write a longer Name.” The content may belong in the Nature, or the object may need a different Type.
> 
> ## 4. Marker and Moniker
> 
> The **Marker [τέκμαρ]** is the opening, logically interpreted feature of the Name. It tells the reader at least the holon's Type and, when Fixed, its reusable identity. The Marker is composed of Code and Cord.
> 
> The **Moniker [τιμή]** is the lexical territory after the Cord. It may be concise, descriptive, eccentric, or highly local. Its freedom is real: the notation can parse a perfectly formed Marker even when the title that follows would puzzle anyone outside the archive. Shared use still rewards clear naming, but clarity is practice rather than parse law.
> 
> ## 5. Code and Cord
> 
> The **Code [μέσος]** is a faceted arrangement of characters. Depending on the Type and Marker form, it can carry typographical, structural, procedural, relational, identity, and state information.
> 
> The **Cord [μέρος]** ends the Marker and opens lexical territory. The core account recognizes two ordinary Cord forms:
> 
> - a space after head punctuation for a **Free [ἀδέσμιος]** Marker;
> - a right colon after the Code for a **Fixed [δέσμιος]** Marker.
> 
> A Free Marker identifies Type without establishing a unique reusable ID for that instance. A Fixed Marker gives the Code durable identity within its governing context. Other hybrid configurations exist for some later Types, but they are outside the minimum anatomy needed here.
> 
> ## 6. Logical and lexical interpretation
> 
> **Logical [λογικός]** and **lexical [λεξικός]** are modes of interpretation, not a division between machines and people. A person can read a period as a formal Term marker. A machine can process natural-language words in a Moniker. The difference concerns what the characters are doing at that moment.
> 
> In logical mode, a character may function as code, identifier, connector, operator, modifier, or separator. In lexical mode, characters function as language and ordinary punctuation. The Name is powerful because one line can cross that threshold in a controlled way.
> 
> ## 7. Definition and Description
> 
> A **Definition [ἐξήγημα]** is an optional inline explanatory feature introduced by a colon-space in lexical territory. It lets a Name carry a short identifying statement without requiring a Nature. For Term holons, a Name-level Definition is normally required because defining the lexical item is the Term's work.
> 
> A **Description [ἑρμηνεία]** is optional bracketed material offering another way of referring to what precedes it. Depending on context, it may hold a translation, transliteration, synonym, etymological descendant, grammatical note, inflection, pronunciation, or controlled glyph. Its scope normally falls on the nearest preceding unit, but placement can make it apply to a larger phrase or the whole Name.
> 
> Definition and Description can nest within lexical material. The same punctuation habits may also appear in an Explanation as ordinary lexical structures. That does not turn them into extra top-level fields.
> 
> The crucial colon distinction is positional and modal. A right colon that completes a logically read Marker is a Cord. A colon-space encountered after lexical territory begins introduces a Definition. The glyph is the same; its neighborhood changes its work.
> 
> ## 8. Explanation and Extension
> 
> The **Explanation** is the main content of a Nature. It may contain prose, data, argument, history, instructions, or whatever the holon's Type and purpose require.
> 
> The **Extension [ἁρμολογία]** is the connective portion of that same Nature. Cory's clearest analogy is a reference article: the Explanation is the article proper; the Extension begins when the article gives way to citations and “see also” material. Explanation and Extension are functional zones, not mandatory sub-fields.
> 
> A Nature may contain only Explanation, only Extension, both, or neither because the Nature itself may be absent.
> 
> ## 9. Reference and Relevancy
> 
> A **Reference [μνεία]** points outside the current information environment: a book, website, article, dataset, artifact, or other source.
> 
> A **Relevancy [μνῆμα]** points inward to another holon as reading guidance. It says, in effect, “this will help you understand or continue from here.” A Relevancy does not automatically create a formal Bond. This prevents the graph from becoming crowded merely because an essay's bibliography or “see also” list is rich.
> 
> ## 10. Field, feature, facet, and format
> 
> These four terms work best as nested levels:
> 
> - A **field [φάρος]** is a defined place where data is stored: the Name field, Nature field, or one property field in the attribute block.
> - A **feature [φυή]** is a recognizable constituent or functional slot inside a field or string: Marker, Moniker, Code, Cord, Definition, or Description.
> - A **facet [φάσις]** is one available choice that can fill or configure a feature. A period and comma can be different facets of the Marker Code feature; a space and colon can be facets of the Cord feature.
> - A **format [φόρμος]** states how a field, feature, or property is written and how much strictness its use requires.
> 
> This resolves the apparent overlap between Field and Feature: fields contain data; features organize the internal form of that data; facets are the specific selections made within those features.
> 
> ## 11. Spacing and relation classes
> 
> **Spacing [χώρισις]** carries meaning in logical notation. The source-era vocabulary names five spatial configurations, though they do not all do the same job:
> 
> - **Head [κεφαλὴ]** spacing occurs at the beginning of a line, with nothing to the left and a space to the right. It allows one of fifteen privileged punctuation marks to typify a Free Marker.
> - **Tight [στενός]** spacing places no spaces around the punctuation between codes.
> - **Wide [εὐρύς]** spacing places spaces on both sides.
> - **Left [λαιός]** spacing places a space to the left but not the right.
> - **Right [δέξιός]** spacing places a space to the right but not the left.
> 
> Head spacing typifies. Tight, Wide, Left, and Right express relations between codes. Ordinary grammatical custom supplies the separate lexical use that the five-part list omits.
> 
> The fifteen marks are period, comma, question mark, exclamation mark, semicolon, colon, apostrophe, quotation mark, caret, asterisk, hyphen, underscore, plus, equals, and tilde. Across the four relational spacings, they produce sixty spaced relations: forty-eight **connectors [δεσμός]** and twelve **operators [ἐνέργεια]**. Six prefix **modifiers [μετάνοια]** and six bracket-based **separators [χωρισμός]** bring the complete Relation system to seventy-two.
> 
> These classes belong here because the Marker Code is built from the same literacy. This essay does not attempt the separate job of defining all seventy-two Relations.
> 
> ## 12. Quarantined residue: Expression
> 
> The historical list's **expression [ἀπαγγελία]** is preserved as evidence, not law. It resulted when an early use of *expression* for *explanation* was treated by an AI as a missing formal category and supplied with its own Greek anchor. It has no stable field, feature, or place in the six pairs. The current Twelve-Part Anatomy has Explanation and no thirteenth Expression.
>

> 
> # Stage Two — Knowledge Map of the Twelve-Property Attribution
> 
> ## 1. Anatomy and attribution are different views
> 
> Anatomy describes the possible internal construction of a holon. Attribution records twelve properties *about* that holon in a metadata **block [κορμός]**. A Block is a reusable formatted unit that can be placed into a document or field. YAML is currently the likely implementation, but its exact serialization remains an implementation choice rather than eternal ontology.
> 
> Name and Nature appear in both systems for a reason. The anatomical Name is the actual one-line inscription; the Name property stores that canonical inscription as data. The anatomical Nature is the optional body below the block; the Nature property reports whether that body exists.
> 
> ## 2. Three tetrads
> 
> | Tetrad | Four properties | Governing question |
> | --- | --- | --- |
> | **Being [ὄντα]** | Name, Type, Nature, Tags | What is this holon, and how is it identified? |
> | **Bonding [σύνδεσις]** | Parents, Children, Siblings, Relatives | How does it participate in the holarchy? |
> | **Becoming [γένεσις]** | Awakened, Altered, Accessed, Activity | When has it existed or been handled, and is it participating now? |
> 
> ## 3. Attributes of Being
> 
> ### Name
> 
> The Name property repeats the complete canonical Name string. It is required.
> 
> ### Type
> 
> The Type property records exactly one of the forty-eight holon Types. It is required. *Category* must not be used as a loose synonym here because Category is itself one of those Types.
> 
> The forty-eight Types were historically arranged as four groups of twelve under **will [βούλη]**, **mind [γνώμη]**, **form [μορφή]**, and **soul [ψυχή]**. Those are family or internal-system labels, not four Type values. Mind and Soul remain provisional names.
> 
> ### Nature
> 
> The Nature property reports whether the optional Nature body exists. A boolean is simply a two-value field: yes/no or true/false. The serialization may change; the two-way distinction does not.
> 
> ### Tags
> 
> Tags record overlapping topical labels. They do not replace the single Type or the formal Bonds. Earlier drafts separate multiple Tags with semicolon-space, though the final YAML rules should govern the concrete syntax.
> 
> Name and Type are the true minimum. The system does not require an invented promotion ceremony, full graph placement, a finished Nature, or proof that the holon is “rich enough.” Once Name and Type exist in usable form, the object can participate according to its Activity state.
> 
> ## 4. Attributes of Bonding
> 
> A **basis [βάσις]** is the holon currently held at the center of attention. It is a view state, not a thirteenth property. Around the Basis, Bonding properties may be displayed as a cross:
> 
> | Direction from Basis | Property | Meaning |
> | --- | --- | --- |
> | above | Parents | Wholes containing the Basis as a Part |
> | below | Children | Parts contained by the Basis as a Whole |
> | right | Siblings | co-members sharing a Parent |
> | left | Relatives | any formal relation not reduced to Whole, Part, or co-membership |
> 
> A **bond [πέδη]** is a formal recorded connection. The four property families use four basic Bond relations:
> 
> - a **parent [γεννήτωρ]** contains the current holon;
> - a **child [ἔκγονος]** is contained by the current holon;
> - a **sibling [ἀδελφός]** shares membership under a Parent;
> - a **relative [συγγενής]** carries any other formal relation.
> 
> Relative is not a weak or “soft” bond. It is a precise residual class. A Relevancy in the Nature may remain informal reading guidance; a Relative in the Block is structurally active.
> 
> When an activating holon has no Bonding entries, the system supplies a fallback Parent so the holon does not enter participation as an unplaced object. The project sources agree on the rule but vary in naming the exact fallback location; that target belongs in the implementation specification.
> 
> ## 5. Attributes of Becoming
> 
> ### Awakened — legacy: Arrived [ποιέω]
> 
> Awakened records the first moment the holon exists in a form capable of receiving a timestamp. It is not the date the holon becomes Active. It is immutable.
> 
> At awakening, Awakened, Altered, and Accessed initially receive the same time because creation is both a change and an access.
> 
> ### Altered [τυγχάνω]
> 
> Altered records the latest modification to the holon's Name, Nature, properties, or other governed content. An alteration also counts as an access, so both fields update.
> 
> ### Accessed [ἀλλάσσω]
> 
> Accessed records the latest engagement with the holon, including reading, loading, consulting, or editing. A read updates Accessed without updating Altered. An edit updates both.
> 
> ### Activity [κατάστασις]
> 
> Activity records current participation and future intent. It is not a grade of intellectual quality.
> 
> | State | Participating now? | Active before? | Intended to participate later? | Plain-language project state |
> | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
> | **active [ἐνεργός]** | yes | yes/current | yes | ready and participating |
> | **preactive [προενεργός]** | no | no | yes | not ready yet |
> | **unactive [ἀνενέργητος]** | no | yes | yes | temporarily not participating |
> | **deactive [ἀπενεργός]** | no | either | no | no longer participating |
> 
> Deactive does not require a past Active period; a Preactive holon may be abandoned before activation. The governing fact is present intent. None of these states calls for deletion. A retired object can remain available for history, provenance, and graph integrity without participating in current work.
> 
> ## 6. Event behavior
> 
> | Event | Awakened | Altered | Accessed | Activity |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | first recordable existence | set once | set | set | set to intended starting state |
> | read or load | unchanged | unchanged | update | unchanged |
> | edit | unchanged | update | update | unchanged unless participation also changes |
> | activate | unchanged | update if metadata changes | update | Active |
> | temporary withdrawal | unchanged | update | update | Unactive |
> | final retirement | unchanged | update | update | Deactive |
> 
> Contact glyphs may be appended to the three timestamps as optional authorship signatures. Their ordering preserves a compact lineage of creation, modification, and use. They enrich the properties without becoming extra properties.
>

> # Stage Three — Two Essay Outlines
> 
> ## Outline A — *The Twelve-Part Anatomy of a Holon*
> 
> ### I. Begin with the object that refuses a single scale
> 
> - Establish **holon [ὅλον]**, **whole [ὅλος]**, **part [ὄζος]**, and **object [πρᾶγμα]**.
> - Distinguish vertical **hierarchy [ἰεραρχία]** from inclusive **holarchy [ὅλαρχία]**.
> - State the 1→2→3 conceptual progression: holon; Whole/Part; object/relation/attribute.
> 
> ### II. Teach the two modes of reading before the anatomy
> 
> - Define **logical [λογικός]** and **lexical [λεξικός]** as interpretive modes available to both people and machines.
> - Introduce **format [φόρμος]**, **field [φάρος]**, **strict [σκληρός]**, and **slack [ὀλίγος]**.
> - Reject the false binary that every Name is fully strict and every Nature fully loose.
> 
> ### III. Open the holon at its largest seam
> 
> - Present **name [φάτις]** and **nature [φύσις]**.
> - Explain required one-line identification versus optional multi-line content.
> - Use the name-length diagnostic to show where identification becomes explanation.
> 
> ### IV. Cross the Name's logical–lexical threshold
> 
> - Divide Name into **marker [τέκμαρ]** and **moniker [τιμή]**.
> - Divide Marker into **code [μέσος]** and **cord [μέρος]**.
> - Explain **fixed [δέσμιος]** and **free [ἀδέσμιος]** Markers.
> - Clarify **feature [φυή]** and **facet [φάσις]** through Marker, Code, and Cord.
> 
> ### V. Show how spacing makes familiar punctuation structural
> 
> - Define **spacing [χώρισις]**, **head [κεφαλὴ]**, **tight [στενός]**, **wide [εὐρύς]**, **left [λαιός]**, and **right [δέξιός]**.
> - Separate Head's typifying function from the four relational spacings.
> - Situate **connector [δεσμός]**, **operator [ἐνέργεια]**, **modifier [μετάνοια]**, and **separator [χωρισμός]** without attempting the whole Relation System.
> 
> ### VI. Let the Moniker carry compressed meaning
> 
> - Define **definition [ἐξήγημα]** and **description [ἑρμηνεία]**.
> - Distinguish the right-colon Cord from the lexical definition colon.
> - Explain Description as bracketed alternative attribution and show how scope follows placement.
> - Quarantine **expression [ἀπαγγελία]** as historical residue rather than anatomy.
> 
> ### VII. Enter the optional Nature
> 
> - Divide Nature functionally into Explanation and **extension [ἁρμολογία]**.
> - Present **reference [μνεία]** as outward source and **relevancy [μνῆμα]** as inward reading guidance.
> - Explain why neither Extension nor its two kinds require separate physical fields.
> 
> ### VIII. Conclude with disciplined compression
> 
> - Return to the aim: dense notation at the threshold, free content in the body.
> - Show that structure makes a holon glance-readable without forcing every kind of knowledge into one prose style.
> 
> ## Outline B — *The Twelve-Property Attribution of a Holon*
> 
> ### I. Move from anatomy to attribution
> 
> - Define the metadata **block [κορμός]** as a reusable formatted unit.
> - Explain why anatomical Name/Nature and their properties are related but not redundant.
> - Name the three tetrads: **being [ὄντα]**, **bonding [σύνδεσις]**, and **becoming [γένεσις]**.
> 
> ### II. Being: identify the holon without overbuilding it
> 
> - Follow the current order: Name, Type, Nature, Tags.
> - State Name + Type as the minimum usable record.
> - Locate the forty-eight Types within the source-era families **will [βούλη]**, **mind [γνώμη]**, **form [μορφή]**, and **soul [ψυχή]**.
> - Correct the category error: these four are family/system labels, not individual Types; Mind and Soul remain provisional names.
> - Define the Nature boolean and distinguish Tags from Type and Bonds.
> 
> ### III. Bonding: turn placement into explicit relation
> 
> - Introduce **basis [βάσις]** as the current center of attention and **bond [πέδη]** as formal connection.
> - Define **parent [γεννήτωρ]**, **child [ἔκγονος]**, **sibling [ἀδελφός]**, and **relative [συγγενής]**.
> - Preserve the directional display: up, down, right, left.
> - Insist that Relative is a precise residual bond, not a weak association.
> - Distinguish formal Relative Bonds from prose Relevancies.
> 
> ### IV. Becoming: record existence, change, use, and intent
> 
> - Introduce Awakened while retaining legacy **arrived [ποιέω]** in the historical vocabulary.
> - Define **altered [τυγχάνω]**, **accessed [ἀλλάσσω]**, and **activity [κατάστασις]**.
> - Show the update rules for creation, reading, editing, and state changes.
> - Introduce optional contact-glyph signatures without adding a thirteenth property.
> 
> ### V. Activity: replace the active/inactive binary with history and intent
> 
> - Define **active [ἐνεργός]**, **preactive [προενεργός]**, **unactive [ἀνενέργητος]**, and **deactive [ἀπενεργός]**.
> - Explain the three questions encoded by the four states: participating now, active before, intended later.
> - Reject “Active means perfected.” Active means admitted to present participation.
> - End with preservation: Deactive objects remain part of history rather than disappearing.
> 
> ### VI. Conclude with a living archive
> 
> - Being gives identity; Bonding gives position; Becoming gives time and intent.
> - The block turns a static note into a traceable participant without confusing metadata with the thing itself.
>

> # Stage Four — Draft 0.1 Essays
> 
> ## Draft 0.1 — The Twelve-Part Anatomy of a Holon
> 
> A holon is an information object that is both a whole and a part. It can contain other holons while participating within other holons, and it may do both in several contexts at once. This is why Holonics needs both hierarchy and holarchy. Hierarchy describes the vertical chain of Wholes and Parts. Holarchy retains that chain while also allowing multiple Parents, shared membership, and relations that do not fit above or below.
> 
> The distinction matters because the system is not trying to turn every body of knowledge into one tree. It is trying to give every object a legible identity while leaving its real relations intact. An essay can belong to more than one collection. A person can participate in several projects. A Term can be relevant to a subject without becoming its Child. The holon is built to withstand those changes of scale.
> 
> Every holon has the same potential twelve-part anatomy, remembered as six alliterative pairs: Name and Nature, Marker and Moniker, Code and Cord, Explanation and Extension, Reference and Relevancy, Definition and Description. These twelve are not twelve equally required fields. They form a nested grammar. The Name and Nature are the two great surfaces. The Name contains Marker and Moniker. The Marker contains Code and Cord. The Moniker may contain Definition and Description. The Nature may function as Explanation and Extension, and the Extension may contain References and Relevancies.
> 
> The Name is mandatory. It is one line and tends to be shorter and more format-strict. The Nature is optional. It may continue for as many lines as the object needs and tends to be format-slack. Strict and slack name degrees of constraint, not two sealed worlds. Exact parsing rules live mainly in the Marker and a few metadata delimiters. The Moniker remains open to ordinary language, and a Nature can adopt a strict local template when that helps its purpose.
> 
> This balance keeps the notation from becoming either unreadable code or unstructured prose. A holon's threshold is dense and regular; its body can breathe. If a Name becomes so long that it wraps down the page, that is a design smell. Some of its information may belong in the Nature, or the holon may need a different Type.
> 
> The Marker is the logically interpreted opening of the Name. The Moniker is the lexical body that follows. Logical and lexical do not mean machine and human. They are two ways of interpreting characters, both available to machines and people. In a Marker, a period may function as a Type-bearing symbol. In a Moniker, the same period may simply close a sentence.
> 
> The Marker has a Code and a Cord. The Code is an arrangement of faceted characters capable of carrying Type, identity, structure, relation, procedure, or state. The Cord concludes that Code and marks the crossing into lexical territory. A Free Marker uses head punctuation followed by a space. It identifies Type but does not give the instance a durable identity code. A Fixed Marker ends its Code with a right colon and establishes an ID that can be reused in references and Bonds.
> 
> This is where Field, Feature, Facet, and Format become useful. A Field is a place in which data is stored, such as the Name or Nature. A Feature is an internal functional part, such as Marker, Code, or Cord. A Facet is an available value of that Feature: a period rather than a comma, or a space Cord rather than a colon Cord. Format governs how those choices must be written.
> 
> Spacing is part of that format. Fifteen punctuation marks may occur in Head spacing to typify a Free Marker. The same marks may occur between codes with Tight, Wide, Left, or Right spacing. Head performs one job—typifying—while the other four express relations. Across those four relational spacings, the fifteen marks yield sixty Connectors and Operators: forty-eight Connectors and twelve Operators. Six Modifiers and six Separators complete the seventy-two Relations of a later internal system. The anatomy essay does not need to define all of them, but it must show why a Code can carry so much in so little space.
> 
> After the Cord, the Moniker can use Definition and Description. A Definition begins with a colon-space in lexical territory and adds a concise explanation to the Name. It is especially important for Term holons, whose work is to define lexical material. A Description encloses an alternative attribution in square brackets. It can contain a translation, transliteration, synonym, etymology, grammatical label, inflection, pronunciation, or controlled glyph. Placement determines whether it modifies a word, phrase, or the whole Name.
> 
> The same colon therefore performs two jobs without confusion. When it ends a logically interpreted Marker, it is a Cord. When it appears after lexical territory has begun, it introduces a Definition. The character did not acquire a magical double meaning. Its position and interpretive mode tell us what it is doing.
> 
> Nature supplies the optional long body. Its Explanation contains the main content: the argument, record, account, instructions, history, or prose. Its Extension holds connections. Yet these are not separate physical fields. A Nature can move from explanation into citations under a heading, or the shift can be inferred when prose ends and bibliography begins.
> 
> References and Relevancies divide Extension by direction. A Reference points out of the current information environment to a source. A Relevancy points inward to another holon as useful reading guidance. Relevancy is not the same as a formal Relative Bond. One belongs to the readable connective matter of the Nature; the other belongs to the structural metadata of the graph.
> 
> Finally, Expression does not belong in the anatomy. It appears in one historical sixty-term extraction because an early slip between *expression* and *explanation* was mistaken for a new formal component and enlarged by an AI. It has no stable field, no syntax, and no place among the six pairs. The twelve parts already close without it.
> 
> The anatomy of a holon is therefore a grammar of disciplined compression. The Name makes the object recognizable at a glance. The Marker makes its structure readable. The Moniker lets people name in their own language. The Nature provides room for whatever the object actually needs to say. The system earns density at the threshold so it does not have to police every sentence inside.
> 
> ## Draft 0.1 — The Twelve-Property Attribution of a Holon
> 
> The anatomy of a holon describes what its representation may contain. Attribution describes the holon from another angle: what it is, how it is bonded, what has happened to it, and whether it participates now. These facts are recorded in a Block, likely serialized as YAML, containing twelve properties arranged as three tetrads: Being, Bonding, and Becoming.
> 
> The Attributes of Being are Name, Type, Nature, and Tags. Name records the complete canonical Name string. Type records one of the forty-eight authorized holon Types. Nature reports whether an optional Nature body exists. Tags supply overlapping topical labels.
> 
> Name and Type are the minimum required pair. This is important because several older AI lectures turned the birth of a holon into an invented ceremony involving completed placement, timestamps, and a “structural contract.” Cory's account is simpler. Give the object a properly formatted Name and one Type; then its Activity state can govern whether and how it participates.
> 
> Type is not a “categorical slot,” because Category is itself one Type among the forty-eight. The source-era framework grouped those forty-eight Types into four internal families of twelve named Wills, Minds, Forms, and Souls. Will is not an individual Type, and the names Mind and Soul were already under review because they gained other controlled meanings in later systems. The distinction between the family names and the Types they contain must remain clear.
> 
> Nature appears in the attribution block even when the anatomical Nature does not. In the block, it is a two-value presence report: yes or no, true or false. Its job is to tell a reader or tool whether body text should follow. This is a boolean, which means nothing more mysterious than a field with two possible values.
> 
> Tags do not replace Type. Type is singular and controlled; Tags may overlap. Tags also do not replace Bonds. A topical label may help retrieval without claiming that one holon contains another or stands in any other formal relation to it.
> 
> The Attributes of Bonding are Parents, Children, Siblings, and Relatives. They describe the holon's participation in the holarchy. Their spatial display becomes clearest when one holon acts as the Basis, the current center of attention. Parents appear above, Children below, Siblings to the right, and Relatives to the left.
> 
> A Parent is a Whole that contains the Basis as a Part. A Child is a Part contained by the Basis as a Whole. A Sibling shares a Parent and therefore expresses co-membership. A Relative records any other formal relation. Relative is not a weak catch-all. It is a precise residual class: not Whole, not Part, not co-member, but still formally bonded.
> 
> A Bond is more than a mention in prose. It is a structural connection stored in the appropriate field and available to tools and queries. This is why Relatives and Relevancies must not collapse into one another. A Relevancy says another holon will help a reader. A Relative says a formal relation exists in the graph. Informal guidance may later justify a Bond, but no automatic promotion is required.
> 
> If a holon is activated without any Bonding properties filled, the system supplies a fallback Parent. This keeps participating objects from floating without placement. The exact receiving location has varied in the source descriptions, so it belongs in the implementation rules rather than being guessed into the ontology.
> 
> The Attributes of Becoming are Awakened, Altered, Accessed, and Activity. Older material calls the first property Arrived. Awakened is better because it marks the first recordable coming-into-being of the holon, not its movement into an archive and not its later activation.
> 
> Awakened is written once and remains immutable. Altered updates when the holon's content or metadata changes. Accessed updates whenever the holon is read, loaded, consulted, or edited. At awakening, all three timestamps begin together. Later, a read updates Accessed alone, while an edit updates Altered and Accessed.
> 
> Optional contact glyphs can be appended to these timestamps to mark who created, changed, or used the holon. They supply compact provenance without requiring three more properties. Their formatting can be strict even though their use is optional.
> 
> Activity is the most conceptually dense property because it records participation and intent. There is one participating state and three nonparticipating states. Active means the holon is ready and presently participating. It does not mean philosophically complete, perfectly validated, or beyond revision.
> 
> Preactive means the holon has never been Active but is intended to become Active. It is not ready yet. Unactive means it was Active, has been temporarily withdrawn, and is intended to return. Deactive means it is not intended to participate again. A Deactive holon may once have been Active, or it may have been abandoned while still Preactive.
> 
> The four states answer three practical questions: Is it participating now? Has it participated before? Is future participation intended? This makes them more expressive than one active/inactive switch while keeping the vocabulary small.
> 
> The refusal to delete is part of the logic. Deactive does not mean nonexistent. It means historically present but outside current participation. Old objects can preserve provenance, explain broken Bonds, or show how an idea changed without crowding active searches and workflows.
> 
> The three tetrads therefore give a holon an account of persistence. Being identifies it. Bonding situates it. Becoming records its history, handling, and intent. Anatomy turns information into a legible object; attribution lets that object live in a changing archive without losing where it came from or what it is doing now.
>
